title: Projectile Motion
standard_text: Forces and motion in two dimensions: projectiles launched horizontally and at angles, independence of horizontal and vertical motion, range, and vector components. (summary of the senior secondary Physics curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Physics worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): projectile motion, range and launch angle, projectiles, vector components and horizontal launches. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
key_sub: Horizontal: constant velocity. Vertical: a = 9.8 m/s² down.
body_html:
How to think about it

A projectile moves sideways at a constant velocity (ignoring air resistance) while it accelerates downward at 9.8 m/s². The time in the air depends only on the vertical motion.

For a launch at angle θ with speed v: horizontal component v cos θ, vertical component v sin θ. On level ground the range is greatest at 45°, and angles that add to 90° (30° and 60°) give the same range.

Example

A ball rolls off a table at 2 m/s and lands 0.5 s later. How far from the table does it land?

d = vt horizontally

Answer: 1 m

Example

Which launch angle gives the greatest range on level ground?

Ignore air resistance.

Answer: 45°

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a faster horizontal throw falls more slowly.
  • Using v instead of its components.
  • Thinking the horizontal velocity changes during flight.
